title: I built a Mafia Wars style Three Kingdoms RPG with Claude Code and FLUX in two months. What worked, and the Chinese characters FLUX kept painting
author: hubert-putu
selftext:
Solo dev here. Warlords of the Three Kingdoms is a text RPG for iPhone and Android, in the Mafia Wars style, set in the Three Kingdoms era. I started on Sep 19 and launched on Nov 10. Since then it has had updates most days. Here's how the AI side actually went.

**Code: specs first, agent second.** Claude Code writes the code. I write the decisions. The repo has 61 spec files: the economy, every feature, the analytics events, the design system. Each agent session has to read the relevant specs before touching code, and if the code ends up different from the spec, the spec gets updated in the same commit. That one rule stopped most of the drift where the agent "remembers" a design differently from last week. I run several agent sessions in parallel, each in its own git worktree, and they all push to main.

**Tests passing is not the game working.** My most expensive lesson. Plenty of bugs passed every test: a sheet that never opened, a first frame painted in the wrong colour, a database index that existed only on the emulator. Now a screen isn't done until the agent has built it, run it in the iOS simulator, tapped through it and looked at the screenshots.

**Balance by simulation.** There's a simulator that plays hundreds of fake players for 200 days. Before I change a number, I ask the agent what it does to day 30 and day 180. That's how I found that a free player would forge 3 Rare weapons in 200 days, not the 20 or so I wanted.

**Art: FLUX 1.1 pro, about 4 cents a portrait.** All 90 Generals are portraits in one lacquer and gold leaf style. The surprise: FLUX paints invented Chinese characters onto every banner, seal and pillar, and "no calligraphy, no characters" in the prompt does nothing. The fix was FLUX Fill. I mark rectangles over the fake glyphs and repaint just those areas with a plain prompt like "a blank banner" or "plain stone". The prompt must not include the style words, because they bring the calligraphy back. Seals I gave up on and draw with code, since a fake seal nobody can read is worse than none. The UI frames and clan emblems came later from GPT Image on Higgsfield, which can paint on a transparent background, so there's no halo to clean up.

The question I'd put to this sub: how do you keep one art style consistent across hundreds of assets when the model drifts between batches? Mine was a fixed style prefix plus picking by hand, and it still took a lot of rerolls.

Every screen in the video is the real game. [warlord3k.com](http://warlord3k.com)
